what: Reassigning the focal and main roles
title: Bivariate dyadic workflow
text: previous analysis used FM_V1 focal sequence, V1 main variable V2 second variable. bivariate method, analysis roles rather fixed identities. describe dyad completely, roles can reassigned member-variable sequence analyzed turn. data set gives different branches global--local procedure depending focal sequence main variable. example, four role assignments illustrate three branches procedure: complete bivariate cases two V1 focal sequences, partial bivariate case FM_V2, univariate case SM_V2. partial branch therefore demonstrated bivariate example data rather artificial seeded example.
code: analyze_bivariate <- function(label, fm_v1, sm_v1, fm_v2, sm_v2) {   emp <- dyadicMarkov::countEmpBivariate(     chainFM_V1 = fm_v1,     chainSM_V1 = sm_v1,     chainFM_V2 = fm_v2,     chainSM_V2 = sm_v2,     states = 2L   )    case <- dyadicMarkov::bivariateCase(emp, alpha = 0.05)    cat("\n", label, "\n", sep = "")   print(case)    if (identical(case$case, "complete")) {     print(dyadicMarkov::completePattern(emp))   }    if (identical(case$case, "partial")) {     print(dyadicMarkov::partialPattern(emp))   }    if (identical(case$case, "univariate")) {     print(dyadicMarkov::univariatePattern(fm_v1, sm_v1, states = 2L, alpha = 0.05))   } }  d <- dyadic_bivariate_example  analyze_bivariate(   "FM_V1 as focal sequence, V1 as main variable",   d$FM_V1, d$SM_V1, d$FM_V2, d$SM_V2 ) #>  #> FM_V1 as focal sequence, V1 as main variable #> Bivariate dyadic case #> Case: complete #> Alpha: 0.05 #> Dyadic interaction pattern #> Pattern: complete actor on the main, actor partner on the second (D2)  analyze_bivariate(   "SM_V1 as focal sequence, V1 as main variable",   d$SM_V1, d$FM_V1, d$SM_V2, d$FM_V2 ) #>  #> SM_V1 as focal sequence, V1 as main variable #> Bivariate dyadic case #> Case: complete #> Alpha: 0.05 #> Dyadic interaction pattern #> Pattern: complete actor partner on the main, partner on the second (D3)  analyze_bivariate(   "FM_V2 as focal sequence, V2 as main variable",   d$FM_V2, d$SM_V2, d$FM_V1, d$SM_V1 ) #>  #> FM_V2 as focal sequence, V2 as main variable #> Bivariate dyadic case #> Case: partial #> Alpha: 0.05 #> Dyadic interaction pattern #> Pattern: partial actor (B2)  analyze_bivariate(   "SM_V2 as focal sequence, V2 as main variable",   d$SM_V2, d$FM_V2, d$SM_V1, d$FM_V1 ) #>  #> SM_V2 as focal sequence, V2 as main variable #> Bivariate dyadic case #> Case: univariate #> Alpha: 0.05 #> Dyadic interaction pattern #> Pattern: APM (A1) #> Alpha: 0.05 #> States: 2

title: Introduction to dyadicMarkov
text: package separates estimation identification. Estimation summarizes observed sequences empirical transition counts maximum-likelihood transition probabilities. Identification compares observed transition structure restricted transition structures corresponding interpretable patterns interaction. univariate workflow, relevant patterns actor-partner, actor-, partner-independence. bivariate workflow, analysis first identifies global case trivial, univariate, partial bivariate complete bivariate. trivial case subsequent local pattern. univariate case followed univariatePattern() main-variable sequences. Partial complete cases followed partialPattern() completePattern(), respectively.

title: Introduction to dyadicMarkov
text: user-facing workflow organized around seven exported functions: countEmp() computes empirical transition counts one focal sequence univariate dyadic sequence. mleEstimation() estimates transition probabilities empirical count matrices. univariatePattern() identifies univariate interaction pattern. countEmpBivariate() computes empirical transition counts one focal sequence bivariate dyadic sequence. bivariateCase() identifies global dependence case focal sequence. partialPattern() selects local pattern partial bivariate case. completePattern() selects local pattern complete bivariate case.

title: Introduction to dyadicMarkov
text: workflow assumes categorical states coded integers 1 states, equal chain lengths, observations collected fixed intervals, first-order homogeneous transition process. Inputs containing NA rejected; missing observations deleted imputed automatically break construction transition pairs. bivariate functions currently support binary-state case. two binary variables observed two members, previous state described four binary components, producing 2^4 = 16 previous-state combinations. Generalizing workflow beyond states = 2 require extending bivariate restriction structures implementation.

title: Univariate dyadic workflow
text: function univariatePattern() performs univariate identification step. compares unrestricted actor-partner structure actor-partner-restricted structures likelihood-ratio tests. two test outcomes combined classify sequence Actor-Partner, Actor-, Partner-Independence. example, selected pattern stored pattern component. returned object list additional S3 class. can therefore printed summarized, still allowing direct access components.
code: pat_uni <- dyadicMarkov::univariatePattern(   chainFM = dyadic_univariate_example$FM,   chainSM = dyadic_univariate_example$SM,   states = 2L,   alpha = 0.05 )  pat_uni #> Dyadic interaction pattern #> Pattern: PM (A3) #> Alpha: 0.05 #> States: 2 pat_uni$pattern #> [1] "PM (A3)" pat_uni$TEST.AM #>  #>  Likelihood-ratio test, Actor-only model #>  #> data:  Observed vs Estimated #> X-squared = 24.551, df = 2, p-value = 4.666e-06 #> alternative hypothesis: The unrestricted model fits the data better pat_uni$TEST.PM #>  #>  Likelihood-ratio test, Partner-only model #>  #> data:  Observed vs Estimated #> X-squared = 1.8984, df = 2, p-value = 0.3871 #> alternative hypothesis: The unrestricted model fits the data better summary(pat_uni) #> $pattern #> [1] "PM (A3)" #>  #> $alpha #> [1] 0.05 #>  #> $states #> [1] 2 #>  #> $call #> dyadicMarkov::univariatePattern(chainFM = dyadic_univariate_example$FM,  #>     chainSM = dyadic_univariate_example$SM, states = 2L, alpha = 0.05) #>  #> attr(,"class") #> [1] "summary_dyadic_pattern" "list"

title: Univariate pattern identification for dyadic Markov chains — univariatePattern
text: chainFM Vector observed states first member (FM). chainSM Vector observed states second member (SM). states single integer >= 2 giving number states. alpha single number (0, 1) giving significance level. Default 0.05.

title: Univariate pattern identification for dyadic Markov chains — univariatePattern
text: list class c("dyadic_pattern", "list") containing two htest objects (TEST., TEST.PM), string pattern, metadata fields alpha, states, call. remains usable ordinary list.

title: Univariate pattern identification for dyadic Markov chains — univariatePattern
text: Pattern labels summarize structure retained tests: IM (A0) denotes independence pattern, APM (A1) actor-partner pattern, (A2) actor-pattern, PM (A3) partner-pattern.

title: Univariate pattern identification for dyadic Markov chains — univariatePattern
code: chainFM <- c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 1L) chainSM <- c(2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 2L) univariatePattern(chainFM, chainSM, states = 2L, alpha = 0.05) #> Dyadic interaction pattern #> Pattern: IM (A0) #> Alpha: 0.05 #> States: 2

title: dyadicMarkov 0.1.1
text: Added S3 classes print/summary support pattern case identification results. Added S3 classes empirical count matrices MLE transition probability matrices preserving ordinary matrix behavior. Added two synthetic 90-point example datasets package workflow examples. Rewrote workflow vignette around built-univariate bivariate example datasets. Improved internal input validation count, estimation, pattern-identification functions. Updated tests documentation new S3 return objects. Improved validation extreme state-space inputs, non-finite chain values, malformed empirical matrices. Refactored selected internal validation AIC helper code reduce function complexity preserving exported behavior. Improved bivariate count validation coverage unsupported malformed inputs.
